title: SQL Foundations: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY
what_is_it: SQL (Structured Query Language) is how you ask a relational database for data. A SELECT statement names which columns you want, FROM names the table, WHERE filters which rows qualify, and ORDER BY controls what order they come back in.
why_it_matters: Almost every other SQL feature you'll learn - JOINs, subqueries, window functions - is built on top of this basic shape. If you're comfortable with SELECT/FROM/WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT, you can already answer a huge range of real questions about real data.
syntax:
SELECT column1, column2
FROM table_name
WHERE condition
ORDER BY column1 [ASC | DESC]
LIMIT n;
example:
SELECT name, price
FROM products
WHERE price > 30
ORDER BY price DESC;
output:
name       | price
-----------------+-------
 Mechanical Keyboard | 79.99
 Standing Mat        | 45.00
 USB-C Hub           | 34.50
common_mistakes: Forgetting that SQL string comparisons ('Portugal' vs 'portugal') are case-sensitive by default in Postgres, unlike Python's often-forgiving == on already-normalized data. Also, ORDER BY DESC sorts largest-first - it's easy to accidentally write it when you meant ASC (the default), or vice versa.
mini_exercise: Without running it yet, predict what 'SELECT first_name FROM customers WHERE country = \'Portugal\' ORDER BY signup_date;' returns, then check your answer against sql-foundations-01 through sql-foundations-08.
postgres_note: Postgres string comparisons are case-sensitive and locale-aware by default - use ILIKE instead of LIKE, or LOWER(column) = LOWER('value'), for case-insensitive matching.
